review.material: The complete public publisher abstract was read.
review.limitations: The full argument, its particular dualisms and its conclusions were not available for inspection.

evidence.description: Primary publisher abstract for the essay.

sections.title: What it is about
sections.text: Knight uses Kandinsky and Klee’s writings as a framework for considering divisions in computational design. Their resistance to rigid oppositions in art provides the starting point.

sections.title: Question and premise
sections.text: Which apparent either/or choices are helpful, and which obscure how design works? The essay asks whether divisions inherited from debates about abstraction can be reconciled in computational design.

sections.title: Method of argument
sections.text: The public abstract describes a conceptual comparison between twentieth-century art theory and contemporary computational-design debates. It does not describe an experiment.

sections.title: What can be said reliably
sections.text: The essay considers reconciliation rather than simply accepting mutually exclusive categories. The abstract does not identify every opposing pair or provide a checked final resolution.

sections.title: Reading boundary
sections.text: Only the abstract was reviewed. Detailed positions must be checked in the paper; the title alone is not evidence for a formal theorem or an algorithm.

sections.title: A question to carry forward
sections.text: When choosing a design method, ask whether two approaches must exclude one another or could play complementary roles. That is a reading prompt, not a tested finding of this guide.
